notes: Canonical memory-comparison SQL/data/parameters and batch counts; diagnostic, not a cross-core benchmark.
All timing precedes tracing. Allocation tracing disables GC for one query at a time; traced time is never reported.
Core allocation sites exclude Ruby internal objects. Answer digests compare query and execute paths on the first parameter.

results.sql: SELECT sum(score) FROM items WHERE bucket = $1
SELECT bucket, count(*), sum(score) FROM items GROUP BY bucket ORDER BY bucket
SELECT sum((score * 3 + bucket) / (bucket + 1)) FROM items WHERE bucket >= $1
SELECT count(*), count(score), min(score), max(score), sum(score), bit_xor(score) FROM items
SELECT sum(CASE WHEN bucket = 0 THEN NULL ELSE score END) FILTER (WHERE bucket >= $1), min(CASE WHEN bucket = 0 THEN NULL ELSE score END) FILTER (WHERE bucket >= $1) FROM items
SELECT CASE WHEN bool_and(score >= 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, CASE WHEN bool_or(score > 5000) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, bit_and(score), bit_or(score), bit_xor(score) FROM items WHERE bucket >= $1
SELECT score % 100, count(*), sum(score) FROM items GROUP BY score % 100 ORDER BY 1
SELECT count(DISTINCT bucket), sum(DISTINCT bucket) FROM items
